answers.answer: Roll one die per held office card simultaneously; add one per fatigue and one more for Chairman. Modified 1–2 does nothing, 3–4 adds fatigue, and 5+ retires the member to Pensioners, flips the card to Vacant Offices, and returns fatigue to supply. Commanders do not roll office attrition.
answers.evidence: London Season—Attrition: “Chairman also adds one”; “5+: retire.”

answers.answer: Players who retired at least one pensioner select or discard one display card, in descending actual retirement spending (after discounts). Ties go to most total windows including new prizes, then clockwise from PM. The acting player may peek at display blackmails. Do not replace a card during selection; if display empties, skip all remaining eligible players. Then discard every remaining display card and refill exactly three, prestige faceup and blackmail facedown, even if nobody took one. Return unused Pensioners to supplies.
answers.evidence: London Season—Retirements; Prestige: “descending actual total retirement spending”; “refilling exactly three.”

answers.answer: At phase start check where the opportunity marker was. A main action can be taken twice only if the marker already matched it; then move marker onto the chosen action. The latest passed extra-action law may grant one extra action after it, never doubled and never moving the marker. Enlist Writer with at least four vacant offices gives one extra writer once this turn: a doubled Writer action places three total.
answers.evidence: Family: “at least four vacant offices”; “doubled Writer action can place three total.”

answers.answer: After all family actions, while Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant to Court as a Company share and lower Debt by one; repeat. If Debt is gone, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible in order. Initial Seek Share money was paid to the bank, never Company treasuries.
answers.evidence: Family—New Company shares: “pay bank”; “Seeking a share never pays family cash into Company treasuries.”

answers.answer: Fill vacant offices in ascending number on card backs. The designated hirer chooses eligible candidate; a promoted officeholder transfers fatigue to the new card, and their old office card re-enters vacancies in ascending order. Hiring your own family into an ordinary office requires verbal consent from every other player represented in that candidate pool. Chairman election and Commander appointments are Nepotism-exempt. If no candidate or hirer exists, skip; office stays vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.
answers.evidence: Hiring: “ascending number”; “If no candidate exists, or the hirer is vacant, skip the office.”

answers.answer: Former Chairman announces the number of shares needed for a pure majority (more than half). Shareholders may campaign; first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. Move one of winner’s Company shares to Chairman slot and give title marker. If nobody wins, former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including self, without Nepotism consent. If Court is empty, former Chairman automatically returns using a supply member or, if necessary and possible, a prize member (losing its VP); if impossible there is no Chairman. Chairman piece still counts as a Company share for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested.
answers.evidence: Hiring—Chairman election: “still counts as a share”; “cannot be traded or invested in firms.”

answers.answer: For a Company office check, commit cash from that office treasury and pay it to bank; gather dice, subtract penalties, roll, and use the lowest die. 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails and may be retried if resources/office limits allow; 5–6 is catastrophic, ends that office’s actions, returns holder to supply, discards fatigue and flips card to Vacant Offices. Specific Commander/firm procedures can modify this. Do not take an action with no effect or chance of success (e.g. no-ship Trade or Deploy without dice to trigger losses).
answers.evidence: Company Operation—Success checks: “Use lowest die”; “You cannot take a dead action.”

answers.answer: Chairman may add up to three Debt freely, each adding £5 Balance. Each further advance requires consent of players controlling a majority of Company shares (Chairman counts); never exceed Debt track end. Chairman must allocate all Balance to other office treasuries, reducing Balance by each transfer. Borrowing and allocation may be interleaved while respecting borrowing rules; existing office cash stays there.
answers.evidence: Actions—Chairman: “allocate all Balance”; “each +£5 Balance.”

answers.answer: Shipping must spend treasury until £2 or less remains. Lease extra ship for £2; fit a ship from a shipyard for £3, without owner consent; buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Put each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China if created. Extra ships return at Refresh.
answers.evidence: Actions—Manager of Shipping: “Must spend treasury until £2 or less remains”; “only if no ships remain on shipyards.”

answers.answer: President declares home region plus reachable regions through open orders and available ship capacity. Each £1 in Presidency treasury buys one die; subtract one die per declared nonhome region. Failed checks may be retried if affordable; catastrophe removes President; only one successful Trade per President per turn, and its retries cannot be interrupted by another position. On success fill one order per ship as possible within declared regions: first writer at home port, each later order touching a writer placed in this same Presidency Trade; other Presidency writers cannot extend route. Cannot fill another President’s home region. Add listed revenue to Balance, or half rounded down if firm already filled it this turn. President earns £1/order and writer owners £1/writer.
answers.evidence: Presidency operations and Trade: “subtract one per declared nonhome region”; “At most one successful Trade per President per turn.”

answers.answer: Commander may target its Presidency’s home, any associated region, or a region bordering an associated region; cannot target another home or another Presidency’s Company region. A Company region must have unrest or a closed order to make Deploy effective. Exhaust officers/regiments for one die each and local alliances for printed dice; subtract target strength plus all other regions in its empire, counting target once (Company defense strength zero). After every attempt, each owner rolls one die per officer exhausted; each 6 removes that officer. Regiments do not roll loss checks.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy: “After each attempt, owners roll one die per officer exhausted.”

answers.answer: On success loot is £4 per target tower plus faceup loot modifier, minimum surviving participating officers +1 (for Commander). Distribute repeated cycles: Commander family £1 for Commander plus each used surviving officer; other families clockwise £1 per used surviving officer; bank last £1 per used regiment and each alliance piece, regardless of alliance strength. Repeat until distributed. Commander gets one trophy per target tower. For a newly Company-controlled target remove tower/dome and capital flags if applicable, open all its orders, remove unrest, put control token region-side up above associated President and Governor overlay on conquered map region; office card goes to Vacant Offices. No Governor overlay if Governor General. Move outward-facing Elephant fully inside target. Catastrophe returns half Commander-family trophies rounded up and Commander to supply; exhausted officers still check losses. Deploying within an existing Company region to clear unrest/reopen orders uses zero defense penalty, zero trophies, and minimum loot of surviving officers+1.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy: “£4 per target tower”; “Company control procedure.”

answers.answer: Governor takes printed dice pool; each attempt rolls current pool without penalty, then pool drops by one regardless of result. Success gains £1, or £2 if immediately preceding roll failed, then choose exactly one: Build Company ship (first success puts partial ship in Governor’s region, next success completes it into President’s sea zone); Commission regiment into President’s associated Army; or Tax unsplit £2 to Balance or President’s treasury. Each unsuccessful roll adds one regional unrest; catastrophe also removes officeholder. Each Tax after first this turn adds regional unrest. Repeat until stop, no dice, or catastrophe.
answers.evidence: Governors—Administer: “reduces the pool by one regardless of result”; “Each Tax after the first…”

answers.answer: Company pays expenses by reducing Balance £1 per Debt, each officer/regiment in Army, and each sea-zone ship including China (not Commanders). If short, take £5 emergency loans, each advancing Debt one; keep taking them even at max Debt, and new Debt adds no current expense. After loans set Balance zero. One or two loans reduce Standing one; three or more reduce it two. Compare remaining Balance to current Standing expectations; if lower reduce Standing one. Then Chairman may pay affordable dividends at £1/share; if total dividend cash is strictly greater than expectations, advance Standing one.
answers.evidence: Revenue: “continue receiving emergency loans even at maximum Debt”; “Dividends.”

answers.answer: Crisis at Elephant location: for attacks on Company resolve primary attack first, then secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest in Bombay, Madras, Bengal Army order; within each Presidency its Commander chooses associated-region order. Normal primary attack strength is ordinary Invasion/Rebellion strength plus target unrest; each secondary strength is only its own unrest. Foreign Invasion primary uses ordinary die without unrest. Commander must exhaust active Army pieces totaling attack strength, or as much as possible; alliances use printed strength and cannot split. A matched defense removes all attacked-region unrest and gives Commander one trophy; successful defense against normal primary Invasion also removes one attacker tower if possible. Unmatched defense means Crisis succeeds. Vacant Commander: Military Affairs acts, or Chairman if it too is vacant; chooses pieces, gets/loses no trophies. Excess indivisible alliance resolution is explicitly unresolved in summary.
answers.evidence: Events in India—Crisis / Attacks on Company: “primary Crisis first”; “A matched defense removes all unrest”; source gap on excess alliance strength.

answers.answer: A vote at support −1 or less fails: discard law, resolve dilemma If Failed text, Opposition Leader returns token and takes PM dial, new PM moves proposed policy one adjacent space either direction and resolves it. At 0 or higher it passes: place law with passed laws, PM takes passed-law token, resolve selected policy first, then immediate law effects. Voting cards are restored after either outcome. A law causing failure still completes vote before scoring.
answers.evidence: Parliament—Resolution: “−1 or less fails”; “Zero or higher passes”; “policy then immediate law effects.”

answers.answer: In 1758 and Long 1710 at turn start before London Season, PM may call Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on lined space, must call it if either is on starred space. Uses ordinary voting and threshold with exceptions: on pass lower Debt one per two current Debt, set Standing to S, PM takes passed-law token and firms activate; on fail increase Company share scoring value by adjusting Court VP token, max ±3. No policy accompanies this vote; failure neither removes PM nor discards Deregulation law, and PM may vote against. 1813 starts deregulated.
answers.evidence: Deregulation: “may…lined space, and must…starred space”; “No policy accompanies this law.”

answers.answer: To form a firm, only a player managing none may return one eligible Company share to supply or flip a workshop invested, flip family board to charter, place a family member as first share, set Value to leftmost, and take £5 bank money into London treasury. Invest with manager consent by same share/workshop contribution, creating a share and £5 bank to London; can invest up to ten shares, with further contributions still adding £5 but no share. Cannot use Chairman share, shares created this turn (even after trade), or Company shares at all while Standing and/or Debt on lined space. Invested workshops never revert, provide no bonus or Company-failure VP, and stay invested if firm fails.
answers.evidence: Firms—Investments: “Up to ten firm shares”; “Cannot use Company shares at all when Standing and/or Debt on lined space.”

answers.answer: Each firm attempts trade once per turn. Managers secretly choose zone/home port with at least one ship (closed home port allowed) and London bid, or Hobnob. Reveal bids simultaneously, keep strategies secret until matching Presidency begins. At Presidency start before actions firms reveal and roll one die per £1 bid, paying bid to bank; at least one 1/2 permits trade. Initiative is ship count minus successful dice and can be negative. Successful President Trade initiative is same calculation. Lowest initiative fills first; President breaks ties, or if President vacant/never trades, firms fill after Commander/Governors with Chairman breaking ties. Fill open orders up to ships+1, starting at home port and tracing own filled route; each firm fills each order once, may refill others’ orders and Company may refill theirs. Previously filled order gives half printed revenue rounded down. Revenue goes India treasury; advance Value one per full £6 added there that turn.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies and competing trade: “Each firm gets exactly one trade attempt”; “per full £6 added to India treasury.”

answers.answer: Before Company Revenue, firms pay £1 per charter ship plus higher of share count or firm Value, using London and/or India treasury. If unable, dissolve unless rescued: shares to Debtor’s Prison (−1 VP each), ships to shipyards, charter to family side, workshops remain invested. After expenses manager may dividend from India only: £1 per share plus £1 manager. Shareholder can waive any number of shares only with manager consent too. Record total actual cash paid out as dividend marker; active firm paying none records zero, Hobnob retains prior marker. Sweep remaining India money to London.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends: “expenses”; “dividends from India treasury only”; “dissolve unless rescued.”

answers.answer: Components are limited; if supply runs out complete as much as possible. Cash, trophies/passed-law tokens, dice and regiments may use proxies. Company Balance, VP and Vote tracks are unlimited. Information is public, including discards and family cash, except facedown blackmail and temporarily hidden firm strategies/bids during selection.
answers.evidence: Components—Limits: “Components are limited”; “All information…is public except…”

answers.answer: Negotiations may transfer enterprises, facedown blackmail, family treasury cash, Company/firm shares and promise cards. Cannot transfer officeholders, writers, officers, prizes, spouses, trophies, passed laws, played blackmail or PM dial; Chairman piece cannot be transferred. A share transfer is represented by replacing member with new owner’s family piece. Blackmail after use is faceup and cannot be traded.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Negotiation: “Cannot trade…played blackmail”; “replace member with new owner’s family piece.”

answers.answer: Immediate transfers bind; future behavior promises do not, except promise cards can force their guaranteed effect if possible. Cards may be traded to third party or guarantor; follow timing/limits. If multiple simultaneous calls cannot all be fulfilled, guarantor chooses which to fulfill. Resources already activated cannot activate again after transfer (e.g. workshop bonus). No promise calls during Final Scoring.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Negotiation: “if possible”; “guarantor chooses which”; “Transferred resources cannot activate twice.”

answers.answer: For five players add three extra player setup cards; for six add six. Shuffle and deal evenly. Each player takes listed cash, enterprises and positions; office listed means family member in office plus office card to owner, Company share means member in Court, writer/officer/trainee to listed box, Commander to slot without office card, and shipyard with ship in listed sea zone or unfitted on shipyard. Each starting luxury gives 2 VP. Build London display by shuffling prestige and blackmail together and dealing three: prestige faceup, blackmail facedown.
answers.evidence: Setup: “add three extra cards for five players or six for six players”; “Each starting luxury gives 2 VP.”

answers.answer: Game ends after scenario final turn or when Standing reaches failure. Failure during Events completes that phase; failure from legislation finishes vote before scoring. Negotiations, promise calls and blackmail stop once game over except a card explicitly permitting final-scoring use. During all Final Scoring no negotiations or promise calls.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: “failure during Events finishes that phase”; “During all of Final Scoring, no negotiations or promise calls.”

answers.answer: Power equals current enterprise/share Power track value (bottom two positions zero), plus one per passed-law token and trophy, two for PM, and printed power from cards including blackmail either faceup/down and applicable spouse. Most/second VP: final turns 1–3 award 3/1; 4–6 award 5/2; 7–8 award 8/4. Tied first each receive only lower award, no other award; tied second receive none. Overall VP tie breaks by most windows, then clockwise from PM.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions—Power award: “Tied first: only lower award”; “Highest final VP wins. Ties…”

answers.answer: If Company survives, firm shares score according to firm Value and Court Company shares score current Court VP/share; final survival procedure rolls office attrition and retires pensioners without prestige. If Company fails, firm shares still score, Debtor’s Prison applies; Company shares lose Court VP/share and uninvested workshops add 1 VP; draw and resolve one random Company failure card instead of ordinary survival retirements. Invested workshops never return and score neither workshop bonus nor Company-failure VP.
answers.evidence: Scoring; Firm investments: “If Company survived…”; “If failed…”

answers.answer: Spouses cannot be transferred and usually add VP plus permanent restrictions. Taking one may require immediate enterprise/share trades. Retirement discounts are personal, can stack, and each can be used once per London Season and once during Final Scoring; discounts reduce actual spending.
answers.evidence: London Season—Spouses: “cannot be transferred”; “each is usable once per London Season and once during Final Scoring.”

answers.answer: If Violet Effingham or an unpaid tax returns a shipyard, its fitted ship remains in play. That shipyard cannot be purchased while its matching ship remains in play; it becomes purchasable after the ship returns.
answers.evidence: London Season—Returned shipyard rule; Parliament—Tax: “fitted ship stays in play”; “purchase becomes possible after the ship returns.”

answers.answer: Family purchases/enlistments: Enlist Writer puts member in any Presidency Writers box; with ≥4 vacant offices, once-turn extra writer (and doubled main action may yield three). Enlist Officer puts member in Officers-in-Training. Luxury costs £4 to bank, yields luxury, 2 VP while owned and window icon. Shipyard costs £2 to bank, gives matching ship unfitted on shipyard, Shipping power/enterprise, one vote and £1 bonus while fitted. Workshop costs £5 to bank, gives workshop, Manufacturing power, two votes, £1 bonus, and 1 VP on Company failure only if uninvested. Seek Share places member on empty Stock Exchange queue and pays bank £2/£3/£3/£4/£5 by space; it is applicant until later conversion and does not immediately give share.
answers.evidence: Family actions; New Company shares: “Purchase Luxury”; “Purchase Shipyard”; “Purchase Workshop”; “Seek Share.”

answers.answer: If required to place a family piece with none in supply, take a piece from any prize and lose that prize’s printed VP; this also applies to firm-share creation. If no family action is possible, take no action and return opportunity marker to supply.
answers.evidence: Family: “take one from any of your prizes and lose that prize’s printed VP”; “If no family action is possible…”

answers.answer: If Chairman election finds Court empty, former Chairman automatically returns. Place a member from supply; if needed, take one from a prize and lose its VP. If no member can be placed even that way, there is no Chairman.
answers.evidence: Hiring—Chairman election: “If Court is empty, former Chairman automatically returns”; “If impossible, there is no Chairman.”

answers.answer: Chairman hires Director, Shipping, Military Affairs, China, Governor General: Director candidate is current officeholder other than Chairman/Governor, or any writer if all offices vacant; Shipping any writer; Military Affairs Presidential Commander, else any officer, else any trainee; China any writer and is hired immediately at creation. Director hires President from associated writers or Governor; President hires associated Governor from a writer or officer in region (not Commander). If no candidate/hirer, skip vacancy, which remains inactive. Governor General replaces Director and hires the same way as Director.
answers.evidence: Hiring table: “Office | Hirer and candidates”; “If no candidate exists, or the hirer is vacant, skip.”

answers.answer: Successful Special Envoy can either open one closed order in a non-Company region or open China by placing overlay/card and immediately having Chairman hire any writer. May repeat checks, paying £1 treasury per die, no penalty. After all Envoys, Director may make up to two transfers, each one writer or ship between any Presidencies/sea zones including China once created. Cannot transfer while still making Envoys.
answers.evidence: Actions—Director of Trade: “Success either opens one closed order…or opens China”; “After all envoys…up to two transfers.”

answers.answer: Military Affairs first may make up to two transfers of one officer/regiment between Armies, remaining top half; next assigns every trainee to any Army top half; finally appoints Commanders. If slot vacant or some family has more total pieces in Army than current Commander’s family, select from families with most pieces. Chosen officer moves to Commander slot and previous Commander returns to top as officer. Tie with incumbent family does not replace them. Nepotism does not apply.
answers.evidence: Actions—Military Affairs: “Finally appoint Commanders”; “A tie with current Commander’s family does not replace them.”

answers.answer: Each President chooses order among its Commander, Governors and own Trade; each gets opportunity but Commander/Governor may decline. One position completes all actions before next; Trade may be before/after a position but cannot interrupt it. If President vacant, Chairman sets order only and cannot Trade or approve alliance purchases.
answers.evidence: Presidency operations and Trade: “Must allow each position an opportunity”; “Trade…cannot interrupt another position.”

answers.answer: The summary does not specify whether ships used for Trade become exhausted. During Refresh, return writers to associated Presidencies and return filled tokens and Presidency dividers; exhausted Army officers/regiments reactivate. Fitted player ships retain fatigue.
answers.evidence: Presidency Trade; Upkeep and Refresh: “return writers…return filled tokens and dividers”; “Fitted player ships retain fatigue.”

answers.answer: Commander first asks President to approve purchases of printed-price local alliances from that Presidency treasury; move purchased alliance to active/top Army half. When used in Deploy or defense, exhaust whole alliance; strength cannot split across purposes. Refresh exhausts unused active alliances too (does not reactivate them).
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy: “President must approve”; “cannot be split among more than one purpose.”

answers.answer: Deploying in an already Company region to reopen orders or clear unrest has zero Company defense penalty, no tower and thus zero tower trophies. With no tower or faceup loot modifier, loot is the minimum of surviving participating officers +1 for Commander, distributed by normal cycles. Dice penalty is zero because Company defense strength is zero.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy: “Company defense penalty is zero”; “minimum loot of surviving participating officers + 1.”

answers.answer: Governor needs two successful Build results total: first success places partial Company ship in Governor’s region; a later success completes it into the sea zone associated with that Governor’s President. Governor-commissioned regiment goes into that same President-associated Army; it has officer-like strength, loot goes to bank, and it has no officer-loss roll.
answers.evidence: Governors—Administer: “two stages require two successes in total”; “Army associated with the Governor’s President.”

answers.answer: China is created by successful Special Envoy or Envoy to China law; Chairman immediately hires any writer either way. China treasury holds ships, not cash; Shipping and Director may send ships there like any sea zone. They count Eastern for expenses, events, storms and laws. China acts after Bengal and may attempt Trade once.
answers.evidence: Superintendent of Trade in China: “Created by successful envoy or Envoy to China law”; “treasury holds ships, not cash.”

answers.answer: China Trade only if Company regions have at least one export icon; the summary does not authorize trading with none, and does not specify a retry after a failed check (only one attempt). Roll one die per ship. On success count icons in all Company-controlled regions only: Balance gets £4 per icon and Superintendent family gets £1 per icon from bank. Non-Company export icons do not count.
answers.evidence: Superintendent of Trade in China: “After Bengal…once”; “only if…at least one export icon”; “all Company-controlled regions only.”

answers.answer: Governor General law immediately makes all Governors pensioners, removes their overlays and partially built Company ships, returns Governor/Director cards to box; replace Director with Governor General, preserving holder and fatigue and placing ribbon overlay. Conquest thereafter creates no Governor/overlay; printed Company symbols show control. When Company regions are lost, skip Governor Elimination; the summary does not state further loss-triggered Governor procedures for this mode.
answers.evidence: Governor General: “make all Governors pensioners”; “Skip Governor Elimination when regions are lost.”

answers.answer: Governor General first adds £3 Balance per Company region. May repeatedly attempt Govern, paying £1 from own treasury per die, no penalty. Each 6 adds one unrest to every Company region even on success; failure adds another unrest to every Company region. Success grants £1 per Company region and requires exactly one benefit per region: complete Company ship to any sea zone incl China, regiment to any Army, or £2 to Balance/any other office treasury (not own) while adding unrest to a Company region. Tax unrests in same turn must go to different regions. At most one successful Govern per turn; the summary doesn’t state a separate limit on unsuccessful attempts except normal stop/retry conditions.
answers.evidence: Governor General: “At most one successful Govern per turn”; “Every 6 rolled…”

answers.answer: For player-owned ships in storm zone, roll each: 1–2 nothing, 3–4 fatigue if unfatigued or sink if already fatigued, 5–6 sink. Sunk ship returns to shipyard unfatigued. Company and extra ships are exempt. China ships count Eastern. Firm ships use their chosen strategy zone and face storms, except Hobnob ships are exempt.
answers.evidence: Events in India—Storms: “Company and extra ships are exempt”; “Hobnob ships are exempt.”

answers.answer: When an event newly closes an order, return any writer there to owner’s supply; flip filled token to closed. If told to close in a fully closed region, Cascade by closing all open orders directly connected to its orders. If a connected order is already closed, close that region’s northernmost open order instead; if none are open, it too Cascades. A region can initiate Cascade once per event tile but may receive effects from multiple Cascades.
answers.evidence: Events in India—Closing orders and Cascades: “Return any writer on a newly closed order”; “region can initiate a Cascade only once per event tile.”

answers.answer: For region-based event, read back of new top draw-stack tile, not drawn tile. Turmoil closes northernmost open order in that region, Cascading if all closed. Windfall pays owners £1 per writer on orders in that region and every bordering region. Shuffle marches Elephant, then shuffles event tile into remaining draw stack and separately shuffles discards onto top; if draw stack empty, do March last instead.
answers.evidence: Events in India: “normally read the back of the new top tile”; Turmoil/Windfall/Shuffle rows.

answers.answer: Leader: if top-stack region is sovereign, add one tower. If dominated, instead rebel using printed explosion modifier. March Elephant only if it was fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled.
answers.evidence: Events in India—Leader: “Top-stack sovereign region gains one tower. Dominated region instead rebels…”

answers.answer: Peace opens orders connected across Elephant border and adds one tower to each touched non-Company region. If Elephant wholly inside a region, instead opens all that region’s orders and removes its unrest. Then Elephant Marches.
answers.evidence: Events in India—Peace: “If Elephant wholly inside a region…Then March.”

answers.answer: Non-Company Invasion compares attacker’s whole empire strength plus event modifier against defender’s whole empire strength; attacker must be strictly greater, so equal does not win. Success replaces defender flag with attacker dominated flag; taking capital shatters whole defender empire. If attacker has no empire, use available free capital/star and matching small flag; if none available no new empire/flags form. Failure attacker loses one tower.
answers.evidence: Events in India—Invasion Crisis: “must be greater than”; “If attacker had no empire…if none available…”

answers.answer: Non-Company Rebellion compares only rebelling region strength plus modifier with its sovereign capital strength; other empire regions do not count. Must be strictly greater. Success actor becomes sovereign, its flag is removed and all its orders close (Cascade if already closed). Failure removes one tower from the capital.
answers.evidence: Events in India—Rebellion Crisis: “Compare only rebelling region strength…against its sovereign capital”; “Failure removes one tower from the capital.”

answers.answer: On Company region loss, Commander returns half own-family trophies rounded up, then Commander to supply. Roll once per officer in associated Army; each 6 removes that officer. Return Governor card to unused stack and fatigue/member to supply; remove Governor overlay, partial Company ship and unrest. Restore dome with one tower, or Foreign Invasion specified strength, plus appropriate invasion flag. Return control token to region with loot side down and region-symbol side up. Future conquest has no loot modifier and region loses Presidency association. Invasion Crisis closes orders (Cascade if already closed); Rebellion/Foreign Invasion already do. Standing loss escalates by number of regions lost this turn: first −1, second additional −2, etc. Other Company regions are not automatically removed; defend/resolve each separately.
answers.evidence: Events in India—Region Loss: “Standing loss equals number of regions lost so far this turn”; “does not automatically lose any other Company region.”

answers.answer: After successful Invasion Crisis, Elephant moves to successful capital; otherwise it moves to top-stack region. In Company region place it fully inside. In dominated region point it toward sovereign. In sovereign region point across tile’s shape-marked border; if neighbor already dominated by actor choose first clockwise neighbor not so dominated; if all are dominated, use redirect-arrow border toward empire capital.
answers.evidence: Events in India—Elephant’s March: “After successful Invasion Crisis…otherwise top-stack region”; posture cases.

answers.answer: Foreign Invasion targets by storm die: West=Bombay, South=Madras, East=Bengal; all storms means each, none means top-stack region. For each target roll ordinary die for attack strength and resolve Invasion/Company attack; unrest does not add to attack strength or tower level. On success close all orders (Cascade if already all closed), remove target flag and all matching flags if capital, restore dome if Company-controlled, set tower to half attack roll rounded down. March circle-shape only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that was invaded.
answers.evidence: Events in India—Foreign Invasion; FAQ ruling: “ordinary die for attack strength”; “unrest does not add”; order/flag/tower procedure.

answers.answer: PM must draw at least one law. After one or two ordinary non-dilemma draws PM may stop or continue up to three total, then choose any revealed one and discard the rest. Drawing a dilemma forces selection of it and ends drawing immediately. Before voting, move dial clockwise or counterclockwise to first policy space matching law’s bottom icon; that space determines target and consequence.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets: “After one or two ordinary…may stop”; “Drawing a dilemma instead forces selection.”

answers.answer: Before normal tax/window/bonus/power policy, policy target is first matching policy space reached by dial movement. Tax: each family pays bank £1 per target owned; unpaid target returns to supply (including Chairman); returned shipyard’s fitted ship stays and cannot be bought until ship returns; lost prize/luxury loses VP. Window tax adds payment per window on enterprises and prize per family member; unpaid enterprise/prize member returns. Bonus: bank pays each family £1 per target owned. Power: swap target marker with next higher marker; if already highest, swap any other pair.
answers.evidence: Parliament—Policy table: “Each family pays”; “BANK PAYS EACH FAMILY”; “if already highest, swap any other pair.”

answers.answer: Starting with PM clockwise, buy votes using £1 family cash per vote plus printed card votes; each card’s votes usable only once across entire vote, rotate when used until vote resolves. Support tracks unlimited. PM may call another full round or stop after each; round with no votes ends voting. Thus voting must end when a no-vote round occurs or PM stops. Restore used cards after resolution.
answers.evidence: Parliament—Voting: “only once in the entire vote, across all rounds”; “round with no votes must end voting.”

answers.answer: A supporter may later oppose; once a player has opposed, they cannot support during that vote. Biggest opponent holds Opposition Leader; ties keep current holder. With recipient consent, votes may be cast on behalf of someone who already opposed or commits to oppose, adding to their opposition total. PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprise opposition except forced “Vote with my enterprises” promise.
answers.evidence: Parliament—Voting: “A player who voted for may later oppose”; “once opposed, cannot vote for.”

answers.answer: On final turn, pay prize upkeep normally; unpaid prize member returns and its VP is lost. Skip Refresh on final turn. On nonfinal turns, return writers, filled tokens and dividers, return extra ships to supply, reactivate exhausted officers/regiments, exhaust active local alliances, advance turn; fitted player ships retain fatigue.
answers.evidence: Upkeep and Refresh: “On final turn, perform upkeep but skip Refresh”; refresh details.

answers.answer: Each shareholder gets one additional special retirement per London Season, from supply rather than Pensioners, regardless of number of firms. Actual spending may not exceed highest total dividend marker among firms where they own a share; no retirement from a firm with absent or zero marker. Spouse discounts may permit higher printed-cost prize; otherwise normal retirement including prestige eligibility. At start of Final Scoring, after firm scoring, each shareholder may make one special retirement regardless Company success/failure and before normal final-scoring steps; no display cards then.
answers.evidence: Deregulation—Special retirement: “one additional retirement”; “No retirement from a firm whose marker is absent or zero.”

answers.answer: Investments: bank pays £5 into firm London treasury for each contribution; trades put revenue into India treasury. London funds ship fitting (£3 to bank), trade bids, and expenses; a purchase of a player-owned ship already in Company costs £3 unfatigued or £2 fatigued, paid to Shipping treasury. Expenses can use either treasury. Dividends are paid only from India treasury. Family cash cannot be gifted/transferred into or out of firm treasuries; only specified procedures move funds.
answers.evidence: Firms—Investments; Firm strategies; Expenses: “London takes investment cash and funds…”; “Family cash cannot be transferred…”

answers.answer: Firms phase, if deregulated, comes after Family share creation and before Hiring. Investment actions happen first in any order until no one wishes more, then strategies chosen. Manager resolves timing conflicts within their firm; PM resolves between firms.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure; Firms phase: “After Family share creation, before Hiring”; “Manager…within firm; PM…between firms.”

answers.answer: Firm may fit ship from a shipyard for £3 from firm London to bank only with shipyard owner consent. Firm may buy player-owned ship already in Company with owner consent, £3 unfatigued or £2 fatigued, paid to Shipping treasury. It cannot acquire Company or extra ships.
answers.evidence: Firms—Investments, Ships: “with shipyard owner consent”; “Firms cannot acquire Company or extra ships.”

answers.answer: Only a player managing no firm may initiate hostile takeover (managing another firm disqualifies). Obtain consent from holders of majority of target shares. Move target firm’s ships, money and shares to own charter; copy both cube positions. Former manager returns cubes and flips board to family side.
answers.evidence: Firms—Hostile takeover: “manages NO firm at all”; “move firm’s ships, money and shares.”

answers.answer: Managers negotiate merger with consent of every shareholder. Highest Value firm is primary; tied highest firms allow players to choose. Transfer all secondary shares, ships and treasury funds to primary; secondary boards return to family sides. Negotiate transfers and any shares over ten returned with owners’ consent. This is one binding immediate transfer. Primary continuing firm keeps its value/dividend track.
answers.evidence: Firms—Merger: “every shareholder’s consent”; “Highest-value firm is primary”; “shares exceeding ten returned with those owners’ consent.”

answers.answer: Hobnob means no bid, trade or dividends; still pays expenses and retains previous dividend marker for retirement eligibility/cap. Its firm ships are exempt from storms.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies; Expenses: “Hobnob”; “Still pay expenses; retain previous dividend marker”; “Hobnob exempts them [from storms].”

answers.answer: Yes. Emergency investments use normal Company-share/workshop rules even if ten-share cap prevents creating another share: each still contributes £5 to London; pay expenses, lose any leftover rescue cash, and lower Value one space per emergency investment. Same-turn share prohibition persists (cannot invest shares created this turn even if traded away); Chairman share and lined Standing/Debt prohibitions also apply.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends; Firm investments: “even when ten-share cap prevents more shares”; “normal Company-share/workshop rules.”

answers.answer: Emergency merger rescue can merge only with one other firm. The rescuing firm must pay its own expenses first if not yet paid, then cover endangered firm’s unpaid expenses. This differs from normal merger, which requires every shareholder’s consent and transfers secondary holdings/treasury etc.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends: “Alternatively merge with one other firm”; “that firm must first pay its own expenses…”

answers.answer: Voluntary dissolution requires consent of all shareholders. The summary refers to “dissolution destinations below”: in failure dissolution, shares go to Debtor’s Prison, ships return to shipyards, charter to family side. It does not explicitly state separate destinations for voluntary dissolution. Invested workshops do not recover; they remain invested.
answers.evidence: Firms—Voluntary dissolution; Firm expenses: “All shareholders must consent”; “workshops remain invested.”; voluntary destination not specified.

answers.answer: Before ordinary final scoring, in deregulated game each player totals VP from all firm shares across all firms, then rounds that player’s own fractional sum down; deduct 1 VP per own family piece in Debtor’s Prison. Company survival/failure does not change these firm-share values. Value/share: 1 −1; 2 zero; 3–4 one-half; 5–7 one; 8–9 one-and-a-half; 10 two.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions; Firm-track VP table: “before rounding their own fractional total down”; firm track values.

answers.answer: Prize levels per family member: cost £2, upkeep £0, VP 0, windows 0; £4, upkeep £1, VP 2, windows 1; £8, upkeep £2, VP 4, windows 2; £14, upkeep £3, VP 8, windows 3; £20, upkeep £4, VP 12, windows 4. Summary does not give separate qualifying “windows” beyond each prize’s listed window count.
answers.evidence: Setup—Prizes: table “Cost / Upkeep / VP / Windows.”

answers.answer: 1710 starts turns 1 and finishes 5; 1758 starts 3 and finishes 7; 1813 starts 5 and finishes 8; Long 1710 starts 1 and finishes 8. Deregulation can be voted in for 1758 and Long 1710 (Long starts same as 1710); 1813 starts deregulated; standard 1710 has no deregulation procedures.
answers.evidence: Setup—Scenario figures; Scenario table: “Turns” table; “1758…deregulation can be voted in”; Long 1710 row.

answers.answer: 1710: Standing £10 expectations, Debt 0, each office treasury £3, Royal Protection passed, one regiment per Army, no Company ships. 1758: Standing £12 expectations, Debt 3, each treasury £4, Calico Acts passed, one regiment per Army, one Company ship in East Indian, Bengal control token in Bengal Presidency.
answers.evidence: Setup—Scenario figures: 1710 and 1758 rows.

answers.answer: 1813: Standing £10 expectations, Debt 0, each office treasury £3; Military Oversight, Deregulation (Debtor’s Prison side), Calico Acts; two regiments per Army and one Company ship per sea zone. Also place +2/−2 share-value token in Court; create China; place Bombay/Madras/Bengal control tokens in Presidencies; return Governor General law to box and put its office overlay over Director of Trade, using Governor General instead of Director and no Governors. Copy exact India map from scenario reverse.
answers.evidence: Setup—Scenario figures; 1813 adjustments: 1813 row and “In 1813…” paragraph.

answers.answer: Power award by final turn: turns 1–3 first/second 3/1 VP; turns 4–6 5/2; turns 7–8 8/4. Tied-first group receives only lower award each and no other award; tied-second receive none.
answers.evidence: Scoring—Power award: “Most/second awards”; “Tied first…”

answers.answer: Initial Power positions: Social 2, Company shares 1, Shipping 0, Manufacturing 0. Standing expectations spaces £4/6/8/10/12/14/16, with reset S above £10. Deregulation lined Standing spaces £4/6/8 and Debt 5/6/7/8; starred Standing £4 and Debt 8. Summary does not specify the exact physical coordinate of marker S beyond “above £10.”
answers.evidence: Setup—Starting Power; Deregulation: “Standing £4/6/8 and Debt 5/6/7/8 are lined; Standing £4 and Debt 8 are starred.”

answers.answer: Unrest does not increase Foreign Invasion primary attack strength or resulting tower strength. Use ordinary die for attack and halve that roll (round down) to set towers. Event still uses Company-defense procedure and secondary unrest attacks. Orders close on success; Region Loss does not separately close them again for Foreign Invasion.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Foreign Invasion and unrest: “unrest does not add”; “ordinary die for both attack strength and halving”; “avoid closing…twice.”

answers.answer: Mercantile/Diplomatic Connection reduced to zero dice means failure. Company Fraud at start of Revenue: roll one die per your officeholder; reduce Balance by twice highest roll, minimum zero, and take from bank only cash equal to actual Balance reduction (no overdraft payout). Public Demands Impeachment returns member to supply and office card to Vacant Offices. Military Oversight demoted Commander is eligible as an officer for reappointment.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Applicable official errata; Company Fraud ruling: “zero dice means failure”; “actual Balance reduction”; card correction list.

answers.answer: Shared setup: initial Company Balance £5; family VP markers zero; local alliances in named Army boxes; loot tokens money-side up in matching regions. Set India map per chosen scenario card, Turn marker to scenario’s starting date, PM dial arm to matching date.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Set Balance to £5…family VP markers to zero, loot tokens money-side up”; “scenario determines…”

answers.answer: Normal order: London Season → Family → Firms if deregulated → Hiring → Company Operation → Bonuses → Revenue → Events in India → Parliament Meets → Upkeep and Refresh. Firms phase follows Family and precedes Hiring; eligible Deregulation vote is at very start before London. Skip London Season on game’s first turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Each game turn follows…”; “Skip London Season on the game’s first turn.”

answers.answer: Retirements start with Chairman; if vacant, former Chairman acts first, then clockwise. Each player may retire each pensioner to a prize; it is optional, not mandatory. Pay printed cost (held aside until London Season ends, then bank), move member to prize, gain printed VP. Unused Pensioners return to their supplies after Prestige selection.
answers.evidence: London Season—Retirements: “Starting with the Chairman (former Chairman if vacant), clockwise”; “each player may retire each pensioner”; unused return.

answers.answer: No. Whenever an empire loses its last dominated region, remove surviving capital’s starred flag so it is no longer an empire. Applies regardless of cause, explicitly including Rebellion and Company conquest of the last dominated region.
answers.evidence: India terminology: “applies regardless of cause, including Rebellion or Company conquest.”

answers.answer: Each firm share scores by Value: 1 = −1 VP; 2 = 0; 3 = ½; 4 = ½; 5 = 1; 6 = 1; 7 = 1; 8 = 1½; 9 = 1½; 10 = 2. Each player totals all own firm shares across firms before rounding their fractional total down.
answers.evidence: Scoring—Firm-track VP per share: “Value 1 = −1…Value 10 = 2.”
